items.q: The minimal change disease box states 85-90% with steroid responsiveness of 95%; about biopsy it says:
opts: Biopsy at presentation in every child
items.exp: MCD: 85-90%; Rx steroid responsive (95%); no role of biopsy. (Book p758)

items.q: The genetic form of FSGS is unresponsive to steroid; its treatment box lists:
items.exp: FSGS genetic form: unresponsive to steroid; Rx: renal transplantation. MN, IgA: rare. (Book p758)

items.q: Thrombosis (renal vessel thrombosis, CVT, DVT) becomes a risk when serum albumin falls below:
items.exp: If serum albumin <2 g/dl → renal vessel thrombosis, CVT, DVT. (Book p758)

items.q: Listed causes of thrombosis include loss of antithrombin III and of protein C/S in urine, ↑ platelet aggregation, ↑ fibrinogen and ↓ plasminogen; the odd one out is:
opts: Loss of antithrombin III in urine
items.exp: The book lists ↓ plasminogen, not ↑ plasminogen. (Book p758)

items.q: Albumin is corrected (to >2 g/dL) using 20% albumin (20 g/100 ml) at a dose of:
items.exp: 20% albumin: 20 g/100 ml; dose: 0.5 g/kg. (Book p758)

items.q: Besides 20% albumin, the book notes that these can also be used:
items.exp: FFP and egg white can also be used. (Book p758)
